title: `strip_whitespace=True` leaves a space before `)` when the group ends with a WHERE clause
spec:
This is the sqlparse library (Python 3, no dependencies). Run the tests with `PYTHONPATH=. python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests`.

Trailing whitespace before a closing parenthesis is normally removed, but not when the text in the parentheses ends with a `WHERE` condition, such as a subquery.

```python
import sqlparse
sqlparse.format('select * from (select a from b where c = d  ) x', strip_whitespace=True)
```
Expected: `'select * from (select a from b where c = d) x'`
Actual: `'select * from (select a from b where c = d ) x'`

The same with a bare clause: `sqlparse.format('( where foo = bar  ) from', strip_whitespace=True)` should be `'(where foo = bar) from'` but is `'(where foo = bar ) from'`.

`strip_whitespace` should remove all whitespace in front of a closing parenthesis, even when that whitespace sits at the end of a nested group (like a WHERE clause) inside the parentheses.
acceptance: Both reported inputs give the expected output
Regression tests are added and the full test suite passes
